While the filters above punish individual users, escalation watches the whole chat:
if many different users cause violations in a short time (a spam wave), a Twitch chat mode
like slow mode or follower-only is activated automatically to protect the entire chat.
The mode is chosen based on the dominant spam pattern of the wave:
Emote spam → slow > follow > sub (emote-only is excluded — it would legalize the spam)
Fresh accounts / message flooding → follow > sub > slow (locks out throwaway accounts entirely)
Caps/character spam → emote-only > slow > follow > sub (makes text spam impossible)
Only modes enabled below can be chosen — disabled modes fall through to the next preference.

TwitchSentry does not judge a message by: TwitchSentry does not judge a message by how many red flags it trips. It asks whether the message is built like an advertisement. An advert has parts: somewhere to go (Destination), something being sold (Offer), a way to redeem it (Instrument), the random @handle a spam bot signs with (Tag), and wording this channel has seen from spam before (Signature). One part on its own is a coincidence — plenty of ordinary messages have one. Two parts together is an advert. That is what these settings control.

A brand-new account is the one exception: one decisive part is enough for someone who has never spoken here before.
Turn off to let a single decisive part act on its own. Expect more false positives.

A block is not a ban. Banning leaves the follower on your list, while a block removes the follow and stops the account following again. It is also quiet: no mod-log entry to read through after a wave.
Blocking is invisible from the viewer's side, though: they simply cannot follow, and nobody tells them. That is why this ships on Report Only, and why every block is written to the list below and can be lifted with !tsundo.
